title: Where a Pixel Points: The Camera as a Function, and What Its Lens Does to Straight Lines

questions.question: A pixel is found for an object. What does it tell you about where the object is?
questions.explanation: Every point along a line from the camera lands on the same pixel, so how far along it is not in the picture. A pixel is a direction. The distance has to come from the size of something, a second camera, or the floor.

questions.question: A point two metres behind the camera is projected by dividing by its depth. What happens?
options: The depth is negative and the division gives a perfectly good pixel
questions.explanation: The mirror image of the point two metres in front, which is why projection says the point is not visible. A point behind the lens does not appear mirrored, it does not appear. The flag exists so the pixel cannot be mistaken for one.

questions.question: Ignoring a lens with k1 of -0.25 put a point near the corner of a 640 by 480 picture 56 pixels from where it was. Why is it invisible near the middle?
options: The bend goes as the radius to the third and fifth powers
The sensor is smaller in the middle
The lens is flat in the middle
questions.explanation: It is 0.1 of a pixel at a radius of 0.1 and 55.8 pixels at 0.8. At two metres that corner is 22.3 cm of floor. A calibration at the centre of the picture finds almost no distortion.

questions.question: Why does undoing the lens need iteration?
options: The bend depends on the radius of the point being looked for
questions.explanation: The answer is needed to work out the answer; it is guessed, corrected and repeated. One pass left the corner 14.5 px out, five 0.083, twenty 3.5e-10.

questions.question: A lens correction is made by applying the lens model with k1 and k2 negated. How far out is the corner?
options: 18.9 pixels: negating the coefficients looks like an inverse and is not
questions.explanation: The inverse of a polynomial scale is not the same polynomial with its signs reversed.

questions.question: A target 0.2 m wide is measured one pixel too wide. The distance error was 1 cm at 1 m and 0.909 m at 10 m. Why?
options: The target gets smaller as it recedes and a pixel does not
The camera is worse far away
questions.explanation: A pixel is a bigger fraction of it, and the error goes as the square of the distance. At 10 m the target is 10 pixels wide, and one pixel is ten percent of it.
